title: The paper: format, timing and open book with notes
blurb: Know exactly what the Version 2 Practitioner paper looks like, how the marks are spread and how to use your 150 minutes.
question: You have 150 minutes, one scenario booklet, the Official Book and 50 questions. How many marks do you need, where do most of them come from, and how should you pace yourself?

teach.h: One scenario, fifty questions, one book
teach.body: The PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner (Version 2) exam has 50 questions worth one mark each, with no negative marking. You need 30 to pass (60%) and you have 150 minutes. It is open book: you may use the PRINCE2 Agile Official Book, and you may write notes inside it, but nothing else. A separate booklet holds one Project Scenario plus an 'Additional information (People)' section, which is needed for at least one question.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner syllabus v2.0, exam overview

teach.caption: Both official Version 2 sample papers follow this 10 / 22 / 15 / 3 split exactly.

teach.h: The paper runs in syllabus order
head: Section
What it tests
About
rows: Mindset, people, OCM, principles, fix and flex
The seven practices, artifacts and the 11 roles
teach.caption: In the official samples only the practice blocks and PROCESSES carry headings; the opening concepts block and the closing wider context items have none. The concepts block also tests the PRINCE2 Project Management principles, practices and processes that PRINCE2 Agile builds on.

teach.h: Foundation and Practitioner side by side

teach.body: Every question has four options and one answer. Styles are standard, missing word, list (pick the two true statements of four, never worded negatively) and, rarely, negative. Each official sample paper carries 8 to 10 '..., and why?' items, most worded 'Is this an appropriate application of..., and why?', plus 'MOST LIKELY', 'NEXT', 'which role', 'where recorded' and 'which workshop topic' stems. Each question adds its own short situation and must be answered on its own: never carry a fact from one question into another.

items.label: Read the booklet; mark constraints, teams, tensions
Answer in order, about 2.5 min each
Flag any item over 4 minutes and move on
Return to flags; answer every question

teach.caption: This is a study plan, not an exam rule. With no negative marking, a blank answer is a lost mark.

teach.body: Larkspur Rail (scenario AS1) runs Fair Fares as four stages: initiation, then one release per stage. A question says the board has authorized Stage 2 only, and will review the updated release map before deciding on Stage 3. Which principle? Manage by stages: the board authorizes one stage at a time and delegates day-to-day control to the project manager within tolerances. The stem gave you every fact you needed; the booklet only set the scene.

steps.label: Answer from understanding
steps.sub: Then open the book to settle one fact

steps.label: Mark and move on
steps.sub: Flag it if it runs long

teach.text: Old material describes Version 1: a Foundation paper of 50 questions with 28 to pass (55%), and a Practitioner paper built from five question sets with four sets of additional information. Version 2 Practitioner is one scenario plus one people list, 50 questions, 30 to pass. Do not mix the two.

items: 50 questions, 1 mark each, no negative marking, 30 to pass, 150 minutes.
Open book: the Official Book only, and notes written inside it are allowed.
Marks: 10 concepts, 22 practices and roles, 15 processes, 3 wider context.
Each question stands alone: use its own situation, never another question's.
PRINCE2 basics (principles, practices, processes) are tested through the agile lens.

summary: You can now describe the Version 2 Practitioner paper, its 10 / 22 / 15 / 3 mark spread and its question styles, and plan your 150 minutes. You can also apply the PRINCE2 principles, practices and processes that the paper's general concepts section tests.

A.q: Lena is sitting the PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner (Version 2) exam. With five minutes left, four questions remain where she cannot choose between two options. She worries that a wrong answer will cost her marks. What should she do?
options: Leave them blank, as each wrong answer loses half a mark
Choose an option for each, as there is no negative marking
Leave them blank, as the pass mark is set on attempted items
Answer two carefully and leave two blank to limit any losses
A.why: Each question is worth one mark and there is no negative marking, so an answered question can only gain marks.

whyNot.0: There is no negative marking in the Practitioner exam.
whyNot.2: The pass mark is 30 of 50, not a share of the questions attempted.
whyNot.3: Leaving any question blank throws away a possible mark; nothing is lost by guessing.

A.q: Tomasz takes a full mock built to the Version 2 Practitioner format and scores 31 out of 50. His friend says he would have failed the real exam. Is his friend right, and why?
options: Yes, because the pass mark is 33 of 50 (65%)
Yes, because the pass mark is 35 of 50 (70%)
No, because the pass mark is 30 of 50 (60%)
No, because the pass mark is 28 of 50 (55%)
A.why: The Practitioner pass mark is 30 of 50 (60%), so 31 is a pass.

whyNot.0: 65% is not the pass mark for either Version 2 exam.
whyNot.1: 70% is not the pass mark; the Practitioner exam needs 60%.
whyNot.3: 28 (55%) was the Version 1 Foundation pass mark, so the verdict is right but the reason is wrong.

A.q: Larkspur Rail is running the Fair Fares project with PRINCE2 Agile, planned as initiation followed by three release stages. At the end of initiation, the project board authorizes Stage 2 only. It tells the project manager it will review progress and the updated release map at the end of Stage 2 before deciding whether to authorize Stage 3. Which principle is being applied?
options: Manage by exception
Learn from experience
Manage by stages
Focus on products
A.why: Under manage by stages the board authorizes one stage at a time and reviews it before committing to the next (5.2.1.4).

whyNot.0: Manage by exception is about delegating within tolerances; the board here is committing one stage at a time.
whyNot.1: Learn from experience covers seeking and using lessons; the stem is about stage-by-stage authorization.
whyNot.3: Focus on products is about defining outputs and their quality; nothing here concerns product definitions.

B.q: Rafael is preparing for the Version 2 Practitioner exam. He has studied the seven practices in depth but plans to skim the processes and workshops, believing they carry only a handful of marks. About how many of the 50 marks come from the processes section?
options: About 10, or 20%
About 22, or 44%
About 3, or 6%
About 15, or 30%
B.why: Learning outcome 3 (processes and workshops) carries 30%, about 15 questions: roughly 11 on applying processes and workshops and 4 on tailoring.

whyNot.0: 20% (about 10 questions) is the general concepts section.
whyNot.1: 44% (about 22 questions) is the practices and roles section.
whyNot.2: 6% (about 3 questions) is the wider context and AI section.

B.q: Question 12 of a Practitioner paper says the CPO has approved a new epic. Question 31 describes a later iteration and asks whether the project backlog has changed. Priya wants to use the approval from question 12 to answer question 31. What should she do?
options: Answer from question 31's own situation and the booklet
Use the earlier approval, as the questions follow one timeline
Use the earlier approval, as the people list links the questions
Re-read question 12, as questions in one section share facts
B.why: Each question must be answered on its own; information from one question is not used to answer another.

whyNot.1: Questions are not a running story; each sets its own situation.
whyNot.2: The people list is shared background, but facts added in one question do not carry to another.
whyNot.3: Questions under the same heading do not share facts with each other.

B.q: On Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares project, the project manager sets up a way for the board to compare the work actually completed with the release map and to forecast whether Release 1 will still go live by the end of month four. Which practice is being applied?
options: Plans
Risk
Progress
Issues
B.why: Progress monitors and compares actual achievements against those planned and provides a forecast for the objectives (12.1).

whyNot.0: Plans defines the products and the means to deliver them; comparing actuals with the plan is progress.
whyNot.1: Risk manages uncertainties; the stem is about tracking actual against planned.
whyNot.3: Issues controls changes to the baseline; nothing here is a change or a problem.

C.q: During Fair Fares initiation, Larkspur's finance director asks for a fixed list of every feature before agreeing the plan. The project manager instead proposes zero tolerance on the £3.2 million budget and the December end date, with Must have epics fixed and Should and Could haves able to flex. Is this an appropriate application of the 'manage by exception' principle, and why?
options: Yes, because agile gives tolerance on what is delivered, not time or cost
Yes, because the board approves each feature as the teams finish it
No, because tolerances are set for time and cost but not for scope
No, because the finance director is accountable for agreeing scope
C.why: In PRINCE2 Agile, manage by exception allows tolerance on what is delivered and restricts tolerance on time and cost (Table 5.1, Table 3.1).

whyNot.1: Approving every feature is not management by exception; the board delegates within tolerances.
whyNot.2: Tolerances can be set for all seven aspects, and scope is an aspect agile flexes (Should and Could haves).
whyNot.3: The project executive is accountable for the project; the CPO owns the project backlog.

C.q: Kofi plans his Practitioner exam: about 15 minutes reading the scenario booklet, including the people list, then roughly 2.5 minutes per question, keeping 10 minutes at the end to revisit flagged items. Is this an appropriate plan, and why?
options: Yes, because each question is worth two marks and needs care
Yes, because the booklet and people list feed into answers
No, because every question can be answered from its stem
No, because 150 minutes allows only one minute per question
C.why: The scenario sets the context and the people list is needed for at least one question, and the plan fits 50 questions into 150 minutes with review time.

whyNot.0: Each question is worth one mark, not two.
whyNot.2: Stems carry their own situations, but the people list is needed for at least one question.
whyNot.3: 150 minutes for 50 questions is three minutes each.

C.q: Fair Fares at Larkspur Rail involves three teams, a supplier on a fixed-price contract and a machine learning model. Because it is large and complex, the project manager proposes using controlling a stage during initiation so that a short research work package on the matching model can start before the project is authorized. Is this an appropriate application of the 'controlling a stage' process, and why?
options: Yes, because the project manager authorizes the project itself
Yes, because large or complex projects may use it in initiation
No, because the process starts after the project is authorized
No, because the board assigns work to the teams in initiation
C.why: Controlling a stage is normally first used after the project is authorized, but can be used during initiation for large or complex projects.

whyNot.0: The project board authorizes the project, not the project manager.
whyNot.2: That is the usual pattern, but large or complex projects are the stated exception.
whyNot.3: The project manager assigns work through work packages; the board directs.

reteach.title: Think of it as a driving test with a map
reteach.question: If you were allowed one map in a driving test, would you read it at every junction?

blocks.h: The map is for checking, not driving
blocks.body: The Official Book is your map. You drive from understanding: read the situation, decide what it shows, and answer. You stop to check the map only when one fact will settle it, such as a workshop topic. You have about three minutes a question, so a candidate who reads the book for every item runs out of road.

items: Read its own situation; it stands alone.
Check one fact in the book if needed, then move on.

explain.body: There are 50 one-mark questions and you need 30. Wrong answers cost nothing, so answer every question.

test.q: Grace is practising for the Version 2 Practitioner exam and wants to know her margin. If she answers all 50 questions, what is the largest number she can get wrong and still pass?
options: 22 questions
15 questions
20 questions
25 questions
test.why: The pass mark is 30 of 50, so up to 20 wrong answers still leaves a pass.

whyNot.0: 22 wrong would leave 28 marks, which was the Version 1 Foundation pass mark, not this one.
whyNot.1: 15 wrong leaves 35 marks; she could afford five more mistakes.
whyNot.3: 25 wrong leaves 25 marks, below the 30 needed.

explain.body: Candidates sitting in a language that is not their native or working language may be awarded 25% extra time: 188 minutes instead of 150.

test.q: Joao, whose working language is Portuguese, is booked to sit the PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner exam in English and qualifies for extra time. How long will he have?
options: 165 minutes
180 minutes
150 minutes
188 minutes

whyNot.2: 150 minutes is the standard time without the extra allowance.

explain.h: One book, with your notes in it
explain.body: The Practitioner exam allows the PRINCE2 Agile Official Book only. You may write notes inside the book; no other material is allowed.

test.q: Mei is packing for her PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner exam. She has her Official Book with notes written in its margins, a one-page summary sheet, her Foundation course workbook and the PRINCE2 7 manual. Which may she use in the exam?
options: The PRINCE2 7 manual for the core method
Her Foundation course workbook
The summary sheet folded inside her book
Her Official Book with her margin notes
test.why: The exam is open book for the PRINCE2 Agile Official Book only, and notes written inside it are allowed.

whyNot.0: The PRINCE2 7 manual is not permitted; only the PRINCE2 Agile Official Book is.
whyNot.1: Course materials are not permitted in the exam.
whyNot.2: A loose sheet is other material, even if it is tucked inside the book.

explain.body: A list question gives four numbered statements; exactly two are true. The options are pairs such as '1 and 3'. List questions are never worded as negatives.

test.q: A Practitioner question about Larkspur Rail's project dashboard gives four numbered statements and asks which two are correct. Which describes this question style?
options: Options are pairs, such as '1 and 3'
It may be worded as a NOT question
It is worth two marks, one per pair
Any number of the four may be true
test.why: List questions have exactly two true statements, the options are pairs, and they are never negative.

whyNot.1: List questions are never worded negatively.
whyNot.2: Every question is worth one mark.
whyNot.3: Exactly two of the four statements are true.
